chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the meal is placed, say 'Bismillah' (In the Name of Allah), and when you eat, say 'Bismillah' at its beginning and its end, and when it is raised, say 'Al-Hamdulillah' (The Praise is for Allah).
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications to recite before, during, and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the ritual etiquette of dining, emphasizing the sanctification of sustenance through specific invocations. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on transforming mundane acts like eating into acts of worship by anchoring them in divine remembrance from the first bite to the final praise.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umyer, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the meal is placed, so say, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, and when you eat, so say, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> at the beginning of it and at the end of it, and when it is raised, so say, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When the table is prepared say, ‘In the name of Allah.’ When your eating is complete say, ‘In the name of Allah at its beginning and at its end.’ When it is removed say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah.’”
